message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
**My preliminary read is sinus bradycardia—a regular rhythm at about 50 beats/minute—with no obvious acute heart-attack pattern.** An image alone cannot rule out a heart problem.

- **Rhythm:** A normal-looking P wave precedes each QRS, consistent with sinus rhythm.
- **Axis and conduction:** Normal axis; PR approximately 160 ms and QRS approximately 80–90 ms. No obvious heart block or bundle branch block.
- **QT:** Does not appear prolonged after correcting for the slow heart rate.
- **ST/T waves:** Slight upward ST–T contour in the anterior chest leads, which may represent a normal repolarization variant. No convincing reciprocal ST depression or concerning T-wave inversion.
- **Voltage:** Prominent chest-lead complexes, but I would not diagnose an enlarged heart muscle from this tracing alone. [ECG voltage criteria](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/multimedia/table/criteria-for-ecg-diagnosis-of-left-ventricular-hypertrophy)

A rate near 50 can be normal during rest or in physically fit people; symptoms and medications matter. **If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or significant dizziness, seek urgent medical care regardless of this interpretation.**

How old is the person, why was the ECG taken, and were there any symptoms?
